newsitem.title: USA: Oscar nominations - monent of truth for Madonna.
newsitem.headline: Oscar nominations - monent of truth for Madonna.

text.p: In typical Madonna style, the never-shy pop diva said she would be nominated for an Oscar. Now Hollywood will be watching on Tuesday to see if her brash prediction will come true.

Apart from the buzz over whether the singer wins a stamp of approval as a big-screen actress, the Academy Award nominations to be announced on Tuesday are wide open this year, with no single film or actor considered a shoo-in.
Experts predict the nod for best picture will come down to a scrap between films about a fascist dictator's wife, a suspected Nazi spy and a girlie magazine publisher defending freedom of speech.

Madonna's vehicle "Evita" -- the screen version of Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical about the wife of late Argentine dictator Juan Peron -- won three Golden Globe awards last month in a precursor to the Oscars and will be a serious contender.

But musicals are often overshadowed by "serious" dramas at Oscar time, so more likely to walk away with the best picture nod are "The English Patient" -- a story of romantic intrigue set in Nazi-era North Africa and Italy -- and "The People v Larry Flynt" -- about the "Hustler" magazine publisher's battle with the American legal system.
"The English Patient" was nominated for seven Golden Globes by the Hollywood Foreign Press Association, but won only two -- best dramatic movie and best original score.

However the film's two stars, Ralph Fiennes and Kristin Scott Thomas, who were passed over for Golden Globes, were nominated for their performances by the Screen Actors' Guild -- another barometer of Oscar preferences.
On the other hand, "The People v Larry Flynt" won a Golden Globe for its director Milos Forman and also took the best screenplay award from the foreign critics in Hollywood.
Two more sets of honours should also be considered in reading the tea leaves of Academy Award nominations.

The Directors Guild of America named "The English Patient" but not "Larry Flynt" in its nominees for best film. The other four movies on the DGA list? "Secrets & Lies" a Cannes festival winner, "Fargo," "Shine" and "Jerry Maguire," whose star Tom Cruise is expected to get a best actor Oscar nomination.
The Writers' Guild of America nominations for best screenplay include the same four, but "Lone Star" replaced "The English Patient" in the top five list.
Much of the focus at Tuesday's nomination ceremony will be on Madonna and her prediction in December at the London premiere of "Evita".
Asked if she expected a nomination for "Evita" and if it would be a big deal to her, she replied simply: "Yes and yes."

Last month Madonna won the Golden Globe award as best actress in a musical or comedy film, however, she struck out with her peers when the Screen Actors' Guild failed to nominate her for its annual awards.
Apart from her acclaimed role in "Desperately Seeking Susan," Madonna's other attempts to become as successful on screen as she is in music have failed.
If she were nominated for best actress, she would face stiff opposition probably from Scott Thomas and possibly also Juliette Binoche, both for "The English Patient."
The 69th Awards Show from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences is scheduled for March 24 in Los Angeles.
